extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare payment policy analysts, hospital finance officers, and stakeholders/respondents to the IPPS notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and methodological rules CMS proposes and uses to compute FY2027 IPPS national and hospital-specific standardized amounts, including inclusion/exclusion criteria, budget-neutrality adjustments, wage-index and labor-related share rules, and simulation procedures for calculating adjustment factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize base-year per discharge costs to remove specified effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1886(d)(2)(B) and 1886(d)(2)(C) of the Act require updating base-year per discharge costs and then standardizing the cost data to remove the effects of certain sources of cost variations among hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These effects include case-mix, differences in area wage levels, cost-of-living adjustments for Alaska and Hawaii, IME costs, and costs to hospitals serving a disproportionate share of low-income patients. (This is the baseline standardization objective applied when computing standardized amounts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use national labor-related and nonlabor-related shares based on market basket
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, continue to use the national labor-related and nonlabor-related shares (based on the 2023-based hospital IPPS market basket) that were used in FY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under section 1886(d)(3)(E) the Secretary estimates the labor-related share. For FY 2027 CMS proposes a labor-related share of 66.0 percent for national standardized amounts for IPPS hospitals with wage index > 1.0000, and to apply the wage index to a labor-related share of 62 percent for hospitals with wage index ≤ 1.0000. See section III.H of the preamble for full discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute equal national average standardized amount (FY2003 large urban base)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(A)(iv)(II) requires that, beginning with FY 2004, an equal standardized amount be computed for all hospitals at the level computed for large urban hospitals during FY 2003, updated by the applicable percentage increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly CMS proposes to calculate the FY 2027 national average standardized amount irrespective of urban/rural location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update standardized amount using applicable percentage increase per statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B) specifies the applicable percentage increase used to update the standardized amount for inpatient hospital operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to use the 2023-based IPPS operating and capital market baskets for FY 2027 and to reduce the applicable percentage increase by the productivity adjustment. There are four possible applicable percentage increases depending on hospital quality data submission and meaningful EHR user status; see section VI.B of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and recommend update factors with MedPAC consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Although update factors for FY 2027 are set by law, section 1886(e)(4) requires CMS to recommend appropriate update factors (taking into account MedPAC recommendations) and section 1886(e)(5)(A) requires publication of recommendations in the Federal Register for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS's recommendation on the proposed FY 2027 update factors is set forth in appendix B of the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for hospitals in standardized amount calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure only hospitals paid under IPPS are included, CMS applied specific inclusion/exclusion criteria when calculating the standardized amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include hospitals whose last four provider-number digits fall between 0001 and 0879. Exclude CAHs and Rural Emergency Hospitals (REHs) at the time of the proposed rule; exclude hospitals in Maryland (paid under an all-payer model); remove PPS-excluded cancer hospitals identified by provider-number flags (e.g., 'V' in fifth position or 'E'/'F' in sixth). See State Operations Manual cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove effects of geographic reclassification and outlier payments before updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the standardized amount to remove the effects of geographic reclassifications and outlier payments before applying the FY 2027 updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After removing those effects, apply budget-neutrality offsets for outliers and geographic reclassifications based on proposed FY 2027 payment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove prior year's budget neutrality adjustments for certain changes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS does not remove the prior year's budget neutrality adjustments for reclassification and recalibration of DRG relative weights and for updated wage data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is because sections 1886(d)(4)(C)(iii) and 1886(d)(3)(E) require estimated aggregate payments after updates in DRG relative weights and wage index to equal estimated aggregate payments prior to the changes; removing the prior adjustment would not satisfy statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality determination methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget neutrality is determined by comparing aggregate IPPS payments before and after making changes that are required to be budget neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of such changes include MS-DRG classification changes, recalibration of MS-DRG relative weights, wage index updates, and geographic reclassifications. Outlier payments are included in simulations because they may be affected by these parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Medicare Advantage IME payments in budget neutrality calculations (but not in outlier threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: IME Medicare Advantage payments made to IPPS hospitals under section 1886(d) are part of budget neutrality calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, Medicare Advantage IME payments need not be included in the outlier threshold calculation or the outlier offset to the standardized amount because the statute requires that outlier payments be not less than 5% nor more than 6% of total 'operating DRG payments,' which does not include IME and DSH payments. See FY 2011 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule for methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit claims to fee-for-service (FFS) in simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: To capture only FFS claims, include only claims with a 'Claim Type' of 60 and exclude claims with a 'GHOPAID' indicator of 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fields are on the MedPAR file. The GHOPAID exclusion follows methodology finalized in FY 2017 to further ensure capture of only FFS claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove certain separately paid charges from covered charges in modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove pharmacy charges for anti-hemophilic blood factor (indicator '3' and revenue code '0636') and organ acquisition charges (except cases grouping to MS-DRG 018) from the covered charge field for budget neutrality adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue centers 081X-089X are typically excluded from ratesetting; revenue 891 charges were not removed from MS-DRG 018 claims because they were included in the relative weight calculation for MS-DRG 018. A new MedPAR variable for revenue code 891 charges was introduced in April 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, CMS is continuing to remove allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell acquisition charges from the covered charge field for budget neutrality adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment for these acquisition costs is made on a reasonable cost basis for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2020 (policy finalized in FY 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include HRRP and Hospital VBP adjustments in budget neutrality calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments for the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program and the Hospital VBP Program are included within budget neutrality calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both adjustments are applied claim-by-claim by adjusting the base-operating DRG payment amount for individual subsection (d) hospitals, affecting the overall aggregate payment sums. CMS applies proxies based on the prior fiscal year's readmissions and VBP adjustment factors on both sides of the aggregate-payment comparison (method adopted in FY 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Medicare DSH and uncompensated care payments per section 1886(r)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include estimated empirically justified Medicare DSH payments equal to 25% of the amount that would previously have been received under the statutory formula, and include the estimated additional uncompensated care payments (the remaining approx. 75% reduced to reflect uninsured changes) on both sides of the budget-neutrality comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to FY 2014 CMS included estimated Medicare DSH payments on both sides of the comparison; for FY 2014 onward CMS follows section 1886(r)'s modified methodology. Include these amounts when determining aggregate payments for budget neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include estimated supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal hospitals and Puerto Rico hospitals are included on both sides of the budget-neutrality aggregate-payment comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supplemental payments are included in computing all budget neutrality factors described in section II.A.4 of the Addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCH payment modeling includes uncompensated care in comparing Federal vs hospital-specific rates
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine total payments for SCHs, model total hospital-specific rate payments and total Federal rate payments and include whichever is greater; include estimated uncompensated care payments in the comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS continues to use FY 2014 finalized methodology under which uncompensated care payments are considered in the Federal vs hospital-specific rate comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude limited MDH program extension from budget neutrality for FY 2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 extended the MDH program for discharges before Jan 1, 2027 and only ~80 hospitals would receive additional payments for the first quarter of FY 2027, CMS proposes not to include this extension in the total payments for budget neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the proposed rule calculations CMS computed payments under the Federal national rate (not including 75% of the difference between Federal and hospital-specific rates) for these hospitals and accounted for uncompensated care payments in the computation of total payments under the Federal rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include adjustment for hospitals not meaningful EHR users
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to include an adjustment to the standardized amount for hospitals that are not meaningful EHR users in modeling aggregate payments for budget neutrality for FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment is based on prior year's performance and payments for hospitals are estimated based on applicable standardized amounts in Tables 1A and 1B for discharges occurring in FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transfer-adjusted discharges in budget neutrality determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the determination of all budget neutrality factors described in section II.A.4 of the Addendum, CMS used transfer-adjusted discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the discharge unit used in the aggregate payment simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of RCH Demonstration budget neutrality factor
rubrics_metrics.description: In FY 2023 CMS finalized a change to apply the RCH Demonstration budget neutrality factor (if applicable) after all wage index and other budget neutrality factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies the ordering change when calculating budget neutrality; see FY 2023 final rule for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG reclassification and recalibration must be budget neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(4)(C)(iii) specifies that annual DRG reclassification and recalibration of relative weights must be made so aggregate payments to hospitals are not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS normalizes recalibrated MS-DRG relative weights so average case relative weight after recalibration equals average before recalibration, but still applies a budget neutrality adjustment because equalizing average case relative weight does not necessarily achieve budget neutrality with respect to aggregate payments. For FY 2027 CMS used FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments comparing aggregate payments using FY 2026 parameters vs proposed FY 2027 relative weights before applying the 10-percent cap, applying proxy readmissions and VBP adjustments. CMS also applies an adjustor for certain MS-DRG 018 cases (CAR T-cell and other immunotherapies) in these simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-percent cap on MS-DRG relative weight reductions requires budget neutrality adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent 10-percent cap on the reduction in an MS-DRG's relative weight in a given fiscal year (effective FY 2023) is implemented such that the cap does not increase estimated aggregate Medicare payments beyond what would have been paid without the cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To calculate the FY 2027 cap-related budget neutrality adjustment CMS simulated payments comparing proposed FY 2027 relative weights before and after applying the 10-percent cap, applied proxy readmissions and VBP adjustments, applied the MS-DRG 018 adjustor, and applied the previously-derived reclassification/recalibration budget neutrality adjustment before deriving the cap adjustment factor. The computed factor is applied to the standardized amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual wage index updates must be budget neutral (statutory requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(E)(i) requires annual updates to the hospital wage index and that updates/adjustments be implemented in a manner that ensures aggregate payments to hospitals are not affected (budget neutral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS finalized a 66.0 percent labor-related share for discharges on/after Oct 1, 2025 and proposes to continue 66.0 percent for FY 2027. Section 1886(d)(3)(E)(ii) provides that Secretary must employ 62 percent as the labor-related share unless that would result in lower payments to a hospital; accordingly CMS proposes to apply wage index to 62% for hospitals with wage index ≤1.0000 and to 66% for hospitals with wage index >1.000. However, for purposes of computing the budget neutrality adjustment under 1886(d)(3)(E)(i), CMS must compute as if 1886(d)(3)(E)(ii) had not been enacted (i.e., cannot take the 62% favorable rule into account).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational mix adjustment data collection and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(3)(E)(i) provides for the collection of data at least every 3 years on the occupational mix of employees for each short-term acute care hospital, to construct an occupational mix adjustment to the wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS proposes to adjust 100 percent of the wage index factor for occupational mix; see section III.D for description of adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for computing budget neutrality adjustment for wage index/labor-related share changes
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute the proposed budget-neutrality adjustment factor for wage index and labor-related share percentage changes, CMS used FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments and compared aggregate payments under different wage index and labor-related share scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, compare aggregate payments using proposed FY 2027 relative weights with FY 2026 pre-reclassified wage indexes applying FY 2026 labor-related share of 66.0% to all hospitals, versus aggregate payments using proposed FY 2027 pre-reclassified wage indexes applying proposed FY 2027 labor-related share of 66.0% to all hospitals, with proxy readmissions and VBP adjustments applied in both. CMS also applied previously-derived MS-DRG budget neutrality adjustment factors (before cap and cap adjustment) to the payment rates used in the simulation before computing the wage-index budget neutrality factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassified hospitals: wage-index reclassification budget neutrality adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(8)(D) requires adjustment to the standardized amount to ensure aggregate payments after implementing reclassification provisions equal aggregate prospective payments absent those provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS includes §412.103 reclassification hospitals with geographically rural hospitals in rural wage index calculations (excluding dual reclass hospitals per hold-harmless). To calculate the FY 2027 factor CMS simulated payments using proposed FY 2027 labor-related share, relative weights, and wage data prior to reclassifications versus after reclassifications, applying proxy readmissions and VBP adjustments. The reclassifications applied are those listed in Table 2 (reclassification crosswalks). The computed factor is applied to the standardized amount to ensure budget neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: National rural floor budget neutrality adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.64(e)(4) CMS makes an adjustment to the wage index to ensure aggregate payments after implementation of the rural floor are equal to aggregate prospective payments that would have been made absent the rural floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rural floor budget-neutrality adjustment is national. In fiscal years with no hospitals in rural Puerto Rico with wage data, CMS calculates a national rural Puerto Rico wage index based on the unweighted average of the wage indexes from contiguous urban areas. CMS used FY 2025 discharge data to simulate payments without and with the rural floor and applied the derived national rural floor adjustment to national wage indexes to produce rural-floor budget-neutral wage indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed (minimum area) floor is non-budget-neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9831 of the American Rescue Plan Act (added 1886(d)(3)(E)(iv)) established a minimum area wage index (imputed floor) for hospitals in all-urban States and explicitly excluded application of budget neutrality under 1886(d)(3)(E)(i) for the imputed floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2022 and subsequent years CMS applies the imputed floor after the rural floor and does not apply reductions to the standardized amount or wage index to fund the increase in payments to hospitals in all-urban States resulting from the imputed floor; see section III.G.2 for full discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent 5-percent cap on wage index decreases and budget-neutral implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS finalized a permanent policy (effective FY 2023) to apply a 5-percent cap on any decrease to a hospital's wage index from its prior FY (hospital's wage index not less than 95% of prior FY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies this permanent cap policy in a budget-neutral manner by adjusting the standardized amount so that aggregate payments under the cap equal what aggregate payments would have been without the cap. To calculate the FY 2027 cap-related budget neutrality adjustment, CMS simulated aggregate payments with and without the 5-percent cap using proposed FY 2027 labor-related share percentages and proposed relative weights, applying proxy readmissions and VBP adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy (continued approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the FY 2025 interim final action with comment period, CMS removed the low wage index hospital policy and the associated budget neutrality factor from the FY 2025 standardized amounts and is continuing related transition policies for FY 2026 and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details and continuation methodology are discussed in the FY 2025 IFC and subsequent sections of the proposed rule (text continues beyond this chunk).
